title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is handwritten on the back of a typed 1979 thesis-defence notice (André Beyries, Montpellier), which has no mathematical relevance. The handwriting is a short tabulation of stabilisers for the icosahedron, labelled 'cas d'icosaèdre'.

I read the four columns of groups as follows, with rows = vertex, edge, face:
- Column 3 (Z/5Z, Z/2Z, Z/3Z): stabilisers of a vertex, an edge and a face in the rotation group A5 (order 60). The orbits have sizes 60/5 = 12, 60/2 = 30 and 60/3 = 20.
- Column 4 (D5, Z/2×Z/2, S3): the same stabilisers in the full icosahedral group A5×Z/2 (order 120). The orbits again have sizes 120/10 = 12, 120/4 = 30 and 120/6 = 20.
- Column 2 (D5×Z/2, D2×Z/2, S3×Z/2): stabilisers in the full group of an antipodal pair, i.e. of an axis through vertices, edge midpoints or face centres. The counts are 120/20 = 6, 120/8 = 15 and 120/12 = 10.
- Column 1 (D5, Z/2-ish, S3 circled replacing a crossed-out Z/3): stabilisers of these axes in the rotation group. These are D5, D2 and S3, with counts 60/10 = 6, 60/4 = 15 and 60/6 = 10.

The numeric tables on the right record exactly these orbit counts. The pairs 12/6, 30/15 and 20/10 are the numbers of vertices, edges and faces versus the corresponding numbers of axes.

The sketches are:
- a square, a pentagon and an oval, which I take to be polygons with 4, 5 and 1 sides. The oval is probably the 'monogone' of the previous page.
- a hexagon subdivided from its centre into triangles. Its sides are labelled a, b, c, a', b', c' (pairings) and it carries a rotation arrow. This looks like a face in barycentric subdivision, or an oriented polygon with its order-3 or order-6 symmetry and side identifications.

Context: the previous and next pages compute explicit Belyi-type maps P^1 → P^1. These are the 'monogone' map g1(z) = -(z-1)^2/(4z) and the 'bigone' map g2(z) = g1(z^2). The aim is to describe the elementary regular maps and their automorphisms within the Teichmüller-groupoid and dessins project. This page is a quick bookkeeping of the cell stabilisers for the icosahedral regular map, probably needed to handle quotients of the sphere by finite rotation groups and the orbifold or automorphism data of cells.
errors: Column 1, row 2 appears to read 'Z/2Z' (possibly 'Z/4Z'). Under the reading above, the rotation stabiliser of an edge-axis is D2 ≅ Z/2×Z/2, so as written it is either a slip or a misreading.
There are no other substantive errors; all orbit counts (12, 30, 20; 6, 15, 10) are consistent with the group orders.

ideas.what: Stabilisers of vertices, edges and faces (and of their axes) of the icosahedron in A5 and A5×Z/2, with orbit counts
ideas.modern_name: Cell stabilisers / orbit–stabiliser for the icosahedral group; regular map {3,5} automorphism data
ideas.where_published: Regular maps and Platonic solids are discussed in general terms in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this specific table is not published.

ideas.what: Sketches of monogon, square, pentagon and a barycentrically subdivided hexagon with paired sides and a rotation
ideas.modern_name: Oriented polygons with side pairings, flags of a map, automorphisms of a map cell
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in the theory of maps and dessins d'enfants

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine table of classical icosahedral stabilisers and orbit sizes, scribbled beside work on explicit Belyi maps. Nothing new or unpublished of substance.
transcription_corrections: Column 1, row 3: 'Z/3' is crossed out and replaced by a circled S3 (𝔖3).
Column 1, row 2: likely intended D2 = Z/2×Z/2; the handwriting reads like 'Z/2Z' or 'Z/4Z'.
Column 2, row 2: reads D2(?)×Z/2Z, with the '×Z/2Z' written beneath.
Right-hand table: the left block reads 12 / [crossed] 12, 30 / 15, 20 / 10, and the right block 12 / 6, 30 / 15, 20 / 10. The second numbers count axes (antipodal pairs).
The headers 'Nb des cas' and 'Nb de facettes' are uncertain readings. Given the numbers, they may be counts of objects versus axes.
The caption 'pentagone orienté' is uncertain; it may be 'polygone orienté', placed near the oval.
